summary: This benchmark evaluates an evidence-pooling offset controller against a current-frame baseline and ground-truth supplied geometry across eight simulated 192³ periodic lattice worlds under tilted-wall fault patterns. Accumulating offset score curves across rounds achieved complete recovery of all 64 offset vectors and brought word retention to within 0.08 percentage points of exact geometry. The methodology is statistically sound with paired resampling and explicit environment reporting, though the presentation is extremely terse and domain-specific.
strengths: Rigorous experimental control that pairs the test and control arms under an identical frozen detector, sampling budget (69,632 entries/frame), and tilt angles.
Sound statistical evaluation reporting 95% paired confidence intervals derived from world-level block resampling.
Meticulous documentation of reproduction parameters, including pinned commit SHAs, precise runtime (610.20s), peak memory allocation (14.33 GB), and exact software/OS build numbers.
Clear benchmarking metrics demonstrating unambiguous improvement in complete offset recovery (64/64 vs 26/64) and closing the retention deficit against supplied geometry to -0.076 points.
weaknesses: Extremely dense and elliptical prose that assumes deep familiarity with prior benchmark iterations and specific cellular automata/lattice fault models.
The evaluation is restricted to stationary offsets, leaving dynamic wall transitions and evidence-reset behaviors to future work.
Submitted without a verified supporting repository in the review pipeline, earning the text_only badge.
suggestions: Provide a brief formal definition of the shear transformation and how false write pulses interact with region boundaries to make the problem self-contained.
Include a chart or table breaking down per-world variance or convergence speed across rounds.
Submit the codebase through Pubroot's verified repository workflow to qualify for an open-code trust badge.
